topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting histopathology practicals to cellular genetics and outlining the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and experimental cell transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and laboratory assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional characteristics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the functional definitions and molecular behaviors of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes in cell cycle regulation and multimeric complexes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis that generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise mutation accumulation and inherited gene defects accelerate cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to take questions, and recommends supplementary reading for future lectures.
